title: Close isolated worker captures without blocking on retained readers
body:
An unexpected isolated-test worker error stopped its owner but left both capture streams open at `run_modules` return. The existing regression closed them only during fixture teardown. Close the retained captures after process cleanup and worker shutdown, preserving the original exception and reporting individual cleanup failures.

CPython Windows readers can retain buffered-stream locks after the owner exits. The shared finalizer waits at most two seconds in total for those readers, then reports incomplete cleanup without blocking on `close()`. The same finalizer replaces direct closes in the existing module-timeout fallback, retaining status 124 and captured bytes. Process cleanup denial remains explicit and does not attempt to close active captures.

Validation on macOS 27.0, CPython 3.12.7:

- The added pre-teardown assertion fails against unchanged base `4c0a359d88f22f05189d51f48387750b801a45d4`.
- Normal and optimized compatibility: 56 tests with 23 expected platform skips, plus eight failure-order and ten exited-pipe tests, all pass.
- Six new real-process controls exercise started captures, original-error preservation, close failure, process-cleanup denial, a retained buffered-pipe reader after successful owner stop, and the timeout fallback. An unbounded-close mutation is rejected before independent fixture cleanup.
- Git-free normal/optimized replay of the six new controls and eight failure-order tests uses eight exact committed files; source hashes remain unchanged.

[Evidence, reproduction commands, source lineage and open questions](docs/research/isolated-worker-capture-finalization.md). [Canonical claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1472#discussioncomment-19141160).

Native Windows execution remains unrun; the retained-reader control uses a real pipe/thread on macOS. This does not identify or claim to fix PR5046's separate Windows destructor-time `Popen` ResourceWarning. No scientific replay, selected-result change or new κ. Retains Douglas Colkitt and the PR5017/cancellation/POSIX/Windows ownership predecessor attribution. Prepared by JoyboyBrian with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0.

Submission checkpoint: canonical main remains `4c0a359d88f22f05189d51f48387750b801a45d4`, with guidance, selected record and declared source inputs unchanged. Shared complete text coverage includes330 open PR bodies at08:11UTC,4195 Discussion records at08:12UTC and6760 tracked notes; focused changed-source searches found no matching new reservation. Arbitrary diffs and unpublished work remain outside this advisory coverage.

## Hosted check limitation

At exact head3bcb7f2763be15022e930c26856f701a4e385e89, three hosted checks passed. The `isolated-runner-successor` job stopped before replay with `working source drift: certificates/selected-result.json`: its frozen manifest expects SHA256bb2eaa58647b353f88d0aec2eafb9d30df1be53589231b23e12ceef3e4bad129, while unchanged base/current selected bytes hash to6fe0a099b89aa2aed796a13c3a21dafc63f3388ebf397464e44e0451893b9375. The same check-only failure occurs with the exact base4c0a runner. Historical SOURCES/VERIFY and the selected record are identical at base4c0a, canonical81e9 and this head. This pre-existing source-pin mismatch is not a capture-finalization regression and was not suppressed or repinned. The failed hosted replay is not reported as executed or passed.
